newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower on Thursday, pulled down by other markets and by book-squaring before the long week-end, dealers said.
The market will be shut on Friday for a public holiday.
"We have seen sales also in cash, especially in the three- to-five year maturities," a dealer in Madrid said.
He added that the downtrend could continue at the beginning of next week. "The long-bond future can shed a bit more to around 117.50," he said.
The 10-year spread versus Bunds ended at around 63 basis points versus 62 bps at the start this morning.
But dealers and analysts agreed in saying that the long- term spread would remain stuck at these levels for a while.

"Spanish domestic investors are already on holidays. They are still bullish, but at least for a while they won't put more money into this market, at these levels," said Luca Jellinek, bond strategist at Paribas in London.
A weaker peseta was adding selling pressure to the market, but dealers said this seemed to be a temporary effect.
